content: Regulator of G-protein signaling 20 (RGS20) is a protein encoded by the RGS20 gene in humans. RGS proteins, including RGS20, serve as both regulatory and structural components of G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) complexes. These proteins function as GTPase-activating proteins (GAPs) for specific classes of G-alpha proteins, namely the Gi class (e.g., GNAI1, associated with MIM 139310) and the Gq class (e.g., GNAQ, associated with MIM 600998). By enhancing the rate of GTP hydrolysis, RGS20 facilitates the rapid transition through the GTP-binding and hydrolysis cycle. This activity accelerates the kinetics of GPCR signaling and promotes the timely termination of signal transduction. In melanocytic cells, the expression of the RGS20 gene may be regulated by the microphthalmia-associated transcription factor (MITF). RGS20 has been experimentally demonstrated to interact with the G-alpha subunits GNAO1 and GNAZ.
